CHIEF COMPLAINT
Upper respiratory infection.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
59-year-old male presents with upper respiratory infection. Patient reports that over the past week while performing yard work, he developed fatigue and shortness of breath. He attributes this to catching his first cold after reduced mask usage at the end of summer, which has progressively worsened. Shortness of breath occurs primarily with exertion, particularly while lifting and carrying heavy bags of soil during landscaping. Patient reports feeling warm but attributed this to exertion rather than fever. Denies productive cough at this time but anticipates cough may develop. Reports bilateral elbow pain and knee discomfort related to heavy lifting. Denies nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Patient has received both COVID vaccines.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
No seasonal allergies. Reports exertional shortness of breath. Reports sensation of warmth. Reports bilateral elbow and knee pain. Denies productive cough, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Depression, Type 2 diabetes, Hypertension.

MEDICATIONS
Metformin, Lisinopril 20 mg daily.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Married. Wife encourages participation in barre classes for relaxation. Engages in yard work and landscaping. Attends social gatherings including house parties.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs normal, afebrile. Heart sounds strong and regular. Bilateral scattered rhonchi on lung examination, clearing with cough. Mild edema of lower extremities. Bilateral elbow tenderness on palpation.

RESULTS
Chest X-ray: no airspace disease, no pneumonia. Hemoglobin A1c: 8.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Upper respiratory infection/viral syndrome: Presumed viral etiology. COVID test to be sent. Expected to resolve in couple of days. Robitussin prescribed for cough. Ibuprofen or acetaminophen recommended for fever and myalgias.

2. Depression: Patient doing well with non-pharmacologic approach via barre classes. Offered pharmacotherapy or psychotherapy referral. Patient declined at this time; will reassess in few months.

3. Type 2 diabetes: Hemoglobin A1c elevated at 8; goal 6-7. Metformin increased to 1000 mg twice daily. Repeat hemoglobin A1c in 4 months.

4. Hypertension: Well-controlled on current regimen. Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily. Prescription refilled. Lipid panel ordered.

Follow-up appointment in 4 months. Patient to contact if symptoms worsen.
